FYI

From: Pamela L. Reynolds
Sent: Tuesday, April 18, 2017 3:40 PM
To: dat...@ucdavis.edu
Subject: Statistics Seminar Series - Matt Dowle, April 19th


Tomorrow Matt Dowle, author of the data.table package in R, is giving a seminar in Statistics titled "Ask Me Anything." This will be an accessible computation (e.g., not theory) talk and may be of especial interest to those of you who use R. See the attached map for directions to the talk location at the MSB.





STATISTICS STUDENT-ORGANIZEDSEMINAR SERIES

DATE:              Wednesday April 19th, 2017, 11:10am

LOCATION:      MSB 1147 (ColloquiumRoom).

SPEAKERS:       Matt Dowle, Hacker at H20.ia, author of data.table in R

TITLE:              “ Ask Me Anything”

ABSTRACT:     I'll start by reviewing a few simple language-agnostic principles for dealing with large data in a statistical context. Then I'll review data.table syntax, recent developments and leave the floor open for questions.  In my 20 year career I've worked mainly for American companies based in London and have seen many hundreds of CVs.  Print out your CV and bring it along - I'm happy to demonstrate tips and tricks.  If you have ideas and feedback for data.table, please don't hold back.


Join us this Spring 2017 for a series of seminars organized by the graduate students (Ozan Sonmez and Irene Kim) of the Statistics Department at UC Davis. The seminars will be held on Wednesdays at 11:10am, in the Colloquium Room MSB 1147
